Built on our server by brief-feeder from the InsightSentry calendar (via the recorder Worker) every 15 minutes and served at /terminal/econ-calendar.json; this committed copy is the fallback. Times are UTC and only UTC — the renderer converts to the reader’s clock. See tools/econ-calendar.md.

events.note: $39 billion at 5.300%, up from 4.834% last month and the highest since 2000 on CNBC's count. Demand was firmer than the three-year's: the bid-to-cover was 2.77 against 2.71 last time and a 2.52 ten-auction average, and indirect bidders took about 80% of the notes. The ten-year had touched 5.365% earlier in the day, its highest since 2002, and eased to about 5.28% after the result.

All 19 participants supported the September hike and most judged that another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end, though they stressed they approach each meeting with an open mind. Many said a higher path was prudent as insurance against persistent inflation, and inflation risks were seen as tilted up on energy prices and AI-related investment. The minutes gave no date; futures price the 28 October meeting as a hold at about 83%, with December the likelier hike. Treasury yields rose and the ten-year touched 5.365% before easing.

Governor Waller said more rate hikes will be needed to bring inflation down after more than five years above target, but that the timing is flexible and they need not come immediately. Vice Chair Jefferson has also said policymakers may need more time before deciding whether another hike is needed.

The record of the 10 September hike, three weeks before the 29 October decision. Since then euro-area inflation has printed 3.8%, French ten-year yields have neared 5% and the market has cut its ECB path to about two and a half more hikes from three and a half; how the Council weighed higher energy prices against slowing growth is the read.

197,000 against 200,000 expected; the prior week was revised to 199,000. The labour market is the part of the Fed's debate that is not moving: the minutes call it close to maximum employment, and claims have stayed near 200,000.

$22 billion at 5.618%, up from 5.308% last month, with a bid-to-cover of 2.54 against 2.61 last time but above the roughly 2.4 average of recent auctions; indirect bidders took about 72% of the bonds. The thirty-year yield had touched 5.73% in the morning and fell to about 5.60% after the result, and the ten-year closed near 5.23%.
St. Louis, the day after the FOMC minutes. Said on 29 September that policy is still slightly accommodative even after the hike.
The Bank of Canada is at 2.25% and decides on 28 October with a policy report and press conference. A jobless rate at 6.4% is the argument against a hike; oil pass-through is the argument for.

The first October survey. September was 48.1 with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6% and five-year at 3.4%; the New York Fed's survey this week put one-year expectations at the highest in more than three years, so the expectations line is the one the Fed will read.
The first big airline of the season, reporting into jet fuel that has doubled in a year. Guidance on fuel and demand is the read, not the quarter.

howToRead.title: Impact is about how much price moves, not how much the number matters
howToRead.text: A high-impact release is one where the spread widens, liquidity thins and the first move often reverses. That is a statement about market structure at 08:30, not about economics. Plenty of important data is marked medium because the market has already priced it.

howToRead.title: The forecast is the level that matters, not the previous
howToRead.text: Price reacts to the gap between actual and forecast, not to whether a number went up or down. A 5.3% PPI print against a 5.3% forecast is a non-event; the same print against a 4.7% forecast is not.

howToRead.title: Two releases at the same minute are one event
howToRead.text: Agencies batch their releases, so you will often see three or four rows sharing a print time — jobless claims alongside the Philadelphia Fed, import prices alongside retail sales. Nobody trades the smaller one on a morning like that. When you see the same time twice, read the highest-impact row and ignore the others.

howToRead.title: A release-driven wick is not displacement
howToRead.text: Models built on liquidity runs misfire badly on data prints, because the move has no intent behind it — it is an auction gap. If your playbook has no rule about scheduled releases, this page is the argument for adding one.
